findings.issue: The app ships with no tests, no test runner, and no test dependencies; the only protection is the harness-owned acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (@vitejs/plugin-react or in-memory loader tests) with a `npm test` script; start with unit tests for lib/format.ts and lib/pokeapi.server.ts against fixture JSON.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToCards encodes the spec's trickiest rules (alternate-form exclusion at id>=10000, dedupe, hidden-ability OR merge, species mapping) with zero coverage; a refactor can silently unmark 'Hidden ability' or re-admit Mega forms.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with fixture refs covering: an alternate form, a duplicate ref with different is_hidden, an unknown species id, and ordering.

findings.issue: The root ErrorBoundary renders 'Not found' for every thrown error, so an API 500 or network failure presents as a 404; no test distinguishes error paths from not-found paths.
findings.suggestion: Add an error-boundary/loader test that stubs fetch to reject or 500 and asserts a distinct error message; fix the boundary to say something other than 'Not found' for non-404 errors.

findings.issue: Search state is local useState initialized once, so back/forward navigation to a different ?q= leaves input and results desynced from the URL; page clamping on line 46 also silently disagrees with the URL's page param.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that navigates client-side to /?q=... (popstate and Link) and asserts the input value and filtered list match the URL; derive q from searchParams or sync in an effect.

findings.issue: buildIndex derives per-species types and generation membership with silent fallbacks (types ?? [] on line 168, generation ?? "" on line 178); a species missing from the type scan silently disappears from every type filter.
findings.suggestion: Unit test buildIndex with a fixture where one species lacks a type record entry; assert visible behaviour (filter membership, card types) rather than internals.

findings.issue: Move aggregation (min-level dedupe per move|method key, fixed-then-alphabetical method order, level-then-name sort) is untested; the acceptance suite only inspects one Pokémon's rendered tables.
findings.suggestion: Extract the aggregation into a pure function and unit test the ordering/dedupe rules with small fixtures.

findings.issue: Client-side sortable tables implement 'missing values sort last in both directions' and aria-sort toggling with no coverage; sorting is the easiest behaviour to break in a refactor.
findings.suggestion: Component-test MovesTable with rows containing null power/accuracy: click headers, assert row order and aria-sort values.

findings.issue: apiGet's promise cache (cache successful responses, delete-on-failure to allow retry) has no tests; a future 'fix' could cache rejections or leak unhandled rejections.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with a stubbed fetch: failure then success on retry, and concurrent calls sharing one fetch.

findings.issue: Artwork URL falls back to a synthesized spritePatternUrl even when the API reports null, so unshipped artwork renders a broken with a non-empty alt; the null case is untested.
findings.suggestion: Test the loader with sprites.other['official-artwork'].front_default = null and assert no is rendered (or alt handling).

findings.issue: Pure helpers (latestEnglishFlavor's last-English-entry rule and whitespace collapse, humanize, idFromUrl returning NaN on malformed URLs) are the cheapest regression targets and have no tests.
findings.suggestion: A short unit file covering humanize, englishName, dexNumber, latestEnglishFlavor (including \f and \n runs) and idFromUrl.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no test script, no cases — so every score for test quality bottoms out at the rubric's no-tests anchors. This matters more than usual because the riskiest logic (species/type derivation, ref-to-card mapping with hidden flags, URL-state filtering, move aggregation and sorting) sits behind thin browser-level acceptance tests the team doesn't own. The code is well-factored for testability (pure lib/ helpers, loader/component separation), so a focused vitest suite could close the biggest gaps in about a day; until then any data-layer refactor is flying blind.
